html:
Diamonds found in the gravels of Kono district in eastern Sierra Leone in 1930, which became the country's most valuable export and later the fuel of its war.

A British company won a monopoly in 1934, but from the 1950s thousands of diggers flocked to the fields, and smuggling became huge. Under Siaka Stevens the trade was run for the profit of a few. In the civil war the rebels seized the fields and sold stones through Liberia to buy arms, and campaigners named them blood or conflict diamonds. This led to the Kimberley Process of 2003, which certifies rough diamonds traded worldwide. Mining still leaves Kono poor and scarred.
sum: Diamonds found in the gravels of Kono district in eastern Sierra Leone in 1930, which became the country's most valuable export and later the fuel of its war.
